edition.en: Thomas Hutchinson’s Oxford text of the Complete Poetical Works (1914), on Project Gutenberg (eBook 4800)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 4800 所录哈钦森编牛津版《雪莱诗全集》（1914）

basis.en: Published in The Examiner in January 1818; the author died in 1822.
basis.zh: 1818 年 1 月刊于《观察家报》；作者卒于 1822 年。

note.en: Shelley wrote it in a friendly sonnet contest in December 1817. The poem is a chain of witnesses: a traveller tells the poet, who tells us, about a sculptor who read a king’s face better than the king knew it. What survives in the end is not the empire but the carving, and the story about it.
note.zh: 雪莱 1817 年 12 月在一次朋友间的十四行诗比赛中写成。诗是一串转述：旅人讲给诗人，诗人讲给我们，讲的是一位雕刻师，他读懂国王的脸比国王自己还透。最后留下来的不是帝国，而是那件雕刻，以及关于它的故事。

excerpt.orig:
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay
Of that colossal wreck, boundless and bare
The lone and level sands stretch far away.
excerpt.en:
Nothing beside remains. Round the decay
Of that colossal wreck, boundless and bare
The lone and level sands stretch far away.
excerpt.zh:
此外什么也没有留下。在那巨大残骸的
废墟四周，无边无际，空空荡荡，
寂寞而平坦的黄沙伸向远方。
